title: Tidal caustics
description: Sunlit turquoise water casts a drifting lattice on pale pool tiles.
useCase: Bring a sense of water and light to hospitality, swimwear, and aquatic identities.
reducedMotion: A representative frame remains still. Live system preference changes immediately stop the loop; the range control continues to update the still image.
limitations: Requires WebGL 1. A static CSS fallback appears when unavailable or after context loss. Caustic-inspired screen-space light pattern; no physical water mesh or light transport solver.
look: Deep teal water filling the frame, crossed by glowing mint-cyan caustic light lines over faint dark pool-tile grid seams.
motion: A WebGL fragment shader slowly drifts three warped sine layers into a shifting caustic lattice while tile seams wobble; the Depth slider brightens the light and a button pauses.
adapt: The caustics are the `FRAGMENT` shader: its three-pass loop builds the lattice, `u_time` (scaled by .17) sets drift speed, `u_control` from the Depth range scales brightness; retint its `vec3` colours. Keep the canvas lifecycle, `sg-tidal-caustics-fallback` and reduced-motion branch.
